results.summary_before: This design implements a 3-bit wide, 4-position register file using multiplexers for address decoding and data storage. It provides separate write and read addresses, a write enable, and outputs for the read data plus internal state and an inverted write enable. Testing involves setting the data bits and write address with write enable toggled to store a value, then setting the read address to retrieve it. The documentation is concise but sufficient to understand the basic operation.

results.summary_before: This is a tiny logic analyzer that samples a single digital input and displays its current state and edge events on a 7-segment display. It uses a shift register to detect rising and falling edges, and counters to extend the display duration for visibility. The design requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout board, and can be tested using a dip switch as the data input. It is intended as a simple debugging tool for observing signal transitions.

It requires a UART host for communication and provides a basic register access mechanism.

results.summary_before: This is a power test module that replicates the standard Tiny Tapeout test design but includes a PMOS transistor to control power to the module. The PMOS requires an external active-low enable signal. The design passes input signals directly to outputs, allowing verification that outputs toggle when power is enabled. It is used to evaluate the power switching FET on the TT03p5 shuttle.

results.summary_before: This design implements a 4-tap FIR filter with user-configurable coefficients, or default coefficients set to 1. It takes an input signal x[n] and produces output y[n] by multiplying the last four input samples with the coefficients and summing the results. The coefficients can be assigned via switches when the enable signal is high, and a reset sets past values to zero and coefficients to ones. External hardware includes a microcontroller to send the x[n] values, and the design is notable for being a simple digital filter implementation.

results.summary_before: This project is a simple 8-bit ALU with six instructions selected by the three least significant bits of an instruction input. The operations include logical OR, NAND, NOR, AND, addition, and subtraction. The design is based on the Overture architecture from the game Turing Complete. Testing involves applying instructions and data inputs and verifying the 8-bit result output.
